headline: eBay's record quarter disappoints
text: On January 19 eBay reported record fourth-quarter revenue of $935.8 million, up 44%, and 2004 revenue of $3.27 billion, up 51%, with net income of $778 million, and announced a two-for-one share split. But its forecast of $1.01 billion to $1.03 billion revenue for the first quarter of 2005 implies much slower growth.
imageCaption: Meg Whitman speaking at eBay Live, 13 January 2005

headline: Back to growth: profit up 45 percent
text: Schlumberger reported on 25 January that its 2004 revenue rose to 11.48 billion dollars from 10.02 billion, and that income from continuing operations before one-off items was 1.21 billion, 45 percent more than in 2003. It raised its dividend.
imageCaption: A wireline truck at a drilling site

headline: Record profit, full reserves and oil above 50 dollars
text: ExxonMobil reported on 31 January a 2004 profit of 25.33 billion dollars and the highest quarterly profit in its history, 8.42 billion. On 18 February it said it had replaced 112 percent of the oil and gas it produced in 2004, the eleventh year in a row above 100 percent. US crude, about 47 dollars at the end of January, was back above 52 dollars in late February.
source: ExxonMobil press release of 31 January 2005, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408805000026/r013105ex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); ExxonMobil press release of 18 February 2005, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408805000045/r021805ex99.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DCOILWTICO (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: ExxonMobil's refinery at Baton Rouge, Louisiana

headline: Greenspan's 'conundrum': long rates fall while the Fed raises
text: Since June 2004 the Fed has raised its rate target in quarter-point steps from 1 to 2.5 percent, yet long-term rates have fallen: the 10-year Treasury yield averaged about 4.2 percent in February against 4.7 percent last June. On 16 February Alan Greenspan told Congress that the behaviour of world bond markets 'remains a conundrum'. The numbers: the Fed's rate 2.5 percent. Inflation 3.0 percent. Unemployment 5.3 percent.
source: https://www.federalreserve.gov/boarddocs/hh/2005/february/testimony.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GS10 (read 2026-10-03); https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FEDFUNDS, DFEDTAR, DFEDTARL, DFEDTARU, CPIAUCNS and UNRATE (downloaded 2026-10-04)

headline: BHP outbids Xstrata for WMC
text: On 8 March BHP Billiton offered US$6.22 a share in cash, about US$7.3bn, for Australia's WMC Resources, owner of the giant Olympic Dam copper and uranium mine, topping Xstrata's hostile offer by 85 US cents a share. Xstrata had launched its bid in November at A$6.35 a share, valuing WMC at A$7.4bn, and WMC had rejected it as inadequate. WMC's board now recommends BHP's offer.
imageCaption: A BHP locomotive, Australia

headline: Bob Iger chosen to succeed Eisner
text: Disney's board chose its president Bob Iger to succeed Michael Eisner as chief executive when Eisner retires at the end of September. Iger came to Disney with ABC in 1996.
imageCaption: Bob Iger ;;

headline: Howard Stringer becomes Sony's first foreign chief
text: On 7 March Sony said Howard Stringer, the Welsh-born head of its American business and a former president of CBS, will succeed Nobuyuki Idei as chairman and chief executive in June. He is the first foreigner to run a major Japanese electronics company.
imageCaption: Howard Stringer, Sony's first foreign chairman and chief executive

headline: Brabeck becomes chairman as well as chief executive
text: Peter Brabeck-Letmathe became chairman of Nestlé in April while staying chief executive. Combining both jobs is controversial among shareholders who want a separate check on management.
imageCaption: Peter Brabeck-Letmathe (photograph from 2008)

headline: Flipping houses: how ordinary Americans get rich on borrowed money
text: In America a new way to get rich is called 'flipping': buy a house with borrowed money, wait a few months, sell it for more, and buy two. A 22-year-old from Las Vegas tells the magazine Fortune that he bought 15 houses in Phoenix with 150,000 dollars of his own money; seven months later they are worth 3 million instead of 2 million. A couple who started with five houses and 1,000 dollars down on each now own twenty. It works because house prices only seem to rise, by 77 percent in New York, 92 percent in Miami and 105 percent in San Diego since 2000, and because banks ask for very little: almost a third of all new mortgages last year were loans on which the borrower pays only the interest and nothing back, against fewer than two in a hundred in 2001. Nearly a quarter of all homes are now bought by investors, not by people who want to live in them.
source: https://fortune.com/2013/07/14/riding-the-boom-fortune-2005 (Fortune, 2005, republished; read 2026-10-04); https://www.nar.realtor/blogs/economists-outlook/share-of-homes-sold-by-use-2001-to-2010 (search result read 2026-10-04); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip_This_House (search result read 2026-10-04)
imageCaption: Phoenix, Arizona (photograph from 2009)

headline: Ahmadinejad, Tehran's mayor, wins Iran's presidency
text: Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, the little-known conservative mayor of Tehran, defeated former president Rafsanjani in a run-off on 24 June with about 63 percent of the vote. He campaigned as a man of the people against corruption and the old elite. The defeated candidates Karroubi and Rafsanjani complained that mosques, the Revolutionary Guards and the Basij militia had steered votes.
imageCaption: Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, elected president of Iran, June 2005

headline: The Swiss join Schengen as France and the Netherlands reject the EU constitution
text: On 5 June Swiss voters approved joining the Schengen area of passport-free travel and the Dublin asylum system by 54.6 percent. Days earlier, French voters on 29 May (55 percent) and Dutch voters on 1 June (61.5 percent) rejected the proposed European constitution, throwing the EU into a crisis about its direction.
imageCaption: The Schengen Agreement of 1985 on display in the Schengen museum in Luxembourg

headline: Apple switches the Mac to Intel
text: On 6 June Steve Jobs announced that Apple will put Intel processors into its Macintosh computers from 2006, replacing the PowerPC chips from IBM and Motorola. Apple has secretly kept a version of Mac OS X running on Intel chips for five years. Paul Otellini, Intel's chief executive since 18 May, worked to win the deal.
imageCaption: Inside Apple's Developer Transition Kit, a Mac with an Intel processor, June 2005

headline: Jim McNerney becomes chief executive
text: Boeing's board named Jim McNerney, head of 3M and a former GE executive, as chairman and chief executive on 30 June. His predecessor Harry Stonecipher was forced out in March over a relationship with a female executive.
imageCaption: Boeing chairman and chief executive Jim McNerney (right) with US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton

headline: Citigroup pays $2 billion to settle Enron suit
text: Citigroup agreed to pay $2.0 billion to settle the class action by Enron investors, who accused the banks of helping Enron hide its debts. Earlier this year it settled claims over Global Crossing for $75 million.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000095012305007233/y09884exv99w1.txt (Citigroup press release, 10 June 2005; read 2026-10-03); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000095012305002524/y06392exv99w1.txt (2 March 2005; read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A Citibank branch in Chinatown, New York

headline: Siemens gives away its mobile phone business to BenQ
text: Siemens agreed to sell its loss-making mobile phone business to BenQ of Taiwan. Siemens will pay BenQ at least 250 million euros to get the new venture started, in return for a 2.5% stake in BenQ; BenQ intends to keep the German plants and the Munich headquarters.
imageCaption: A BenQ-Siemens mobile phone, model S68

headline: China lets the yuan rise
text: On 21 July China ended the yuan's peg to the dollar at about 8.28, revalued it to 8.11 and said it will now be managed against a basket of currencies. Washington has long complained that the cheap yuan gives Chinese exporters an unfair edge.
imageCaption: A bank teller in Shanghai counts yuan and dollars the day after China let the yuan rise, 22 July 2005
imageCredit: Photo by STR/AFP via Getty Images

headline: Home prices up 15 percent in a year; Greenspan sees 'froth'
text: Americans bought existing homes at a record annual rate of 7.33 million in June, and the median price reached a record 219,000 dollars, 14.7 percent more than a year earlier, the biggest jump since 1980. On 9 June Fed chairman Alan Greenspan told Congress that exceptionally low interest rates on home mortgages were a major factor in the steep climb in home prices, and that there were 'at a minimum, signs of froth in some local markets'. He called the rapid spread of interest-only loans and other exotic adjustable-rate mortgages a particular concern. A 30-year mortgage costs about 5.7 percent.
imageCaption: McMansion, 2005

headline: Amazon's sales grow 26%
text: On July 26 Amazon reported second-quarter sales of $1.75 billion, up 26%, and net income of $52 million, down from $76 million a year earlier. Operating income excluding currency effects grew 27%.
imageCaption: Amazon (photograph from 2015)

headline: Schrempp quits and the shares jump
text: On 28 July DaimlerChrysler said Jürgen Schrempp will step down at the end of the year. Dieter Zetsche, who has turned Chrysler around with models such as the 300C, will take over. Investors had criticised the lagging share price and weak profits at Mercedes; the shares rose almost 10% on the day.
source: NBC News, 'DaimlerChrysler CEO Schrempp to step down', 28 July 2005, https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna8737805 (read 2026-10-03); Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 2005 ('Board of Management chairman: Zetsche follows Schrempp', 28 July 2005), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/2005.xhtml?oid=4913367 (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Jürgen Schrempp, chairman of DaimlerChrysler, in an earlier picture from 1993

headline: Floods in central Switzerland
text: After days of heavy rain, floods and landslides hit central Switzerland and the Bernese Oberland around 22 August. Engelberg, with 4,000 inhabitants and 1,000 tourists, was cut off and could only be reached by helicopter, and two firemen were killed in the Entlebuch by a landslide. Six to ten people died in Switzerland, and damage runs into billions of francs.
imageCaption: A flooded hotel on Lake Ägeri in Unterägeri, canton Zug, August 2005

headline: Hurricane Katrina hits the Gulf oil coast
text: Hurricane Katrina struck the Gulf coast on 29 August. The region supplies about a tenth of US crude and refines almost half its gasoline; on 31 August eight Gulf refineries were still shut. US crude futures topped $70 a barrel, a record, and the government is releasing oil from the strategic reserve.
imageCaption: Hurricane Katrina over the Gulf of Mexico, satellite view, 28 August 2005

headline: Xstrata buys a fifth of Falconbridge
text: Xstrata has bought a 20% stake in Falconbridge, the Canadian nickel, copper and zinc miner, from Brascan. The purchase makes Xstrata Falconbridge's largest shareholder and sets it up for a possible full takeover. Copper is averaging about $3,800 a tonne, double its level of two years ago.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falconbridge_Ltd.; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xstrata; World Bank Pink Sheet monthly averages (all read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Falconbridge's nickel refinery in Kristiansand, Norway

headline: eBay buys Skype for $2.6 billion
text: eBay has acquired Skype, which offers free telephone calls over the internet, for $2.6 billion. eBay plans to tie it into its marketplace.
imageCaption: Niklas Zennstrom, co-founder of Skype

headline: Cisco buys Scientific-Atlanta for $6.9 billion
text: Cisco agreed on November 18 to buy Scientific-Atlanta, a Georgia maker of cable television set-top boxes and network equipment, for $43 a share in cash, about $6.9 billion. Cisco's sales are now about $25 billion a year.
imageCaption: A Scientific-Atlanta Explorer 8300HD cable set-top box with digital video recorder, the kind of product Cisco was buying

headline: 2005 in review: a flat year under rising rates
text: The S&P 500 rose only 3% in 2005 to 1,248.29, and the Dow slipped 0.6%. The Federal Reserve raised its key rate at every meeting of the year, eight times, to 4.25 percent.
imageCaption: American shares (S&P 500) at the end of each month of 2005: up 3 percent in the year
imageCredit: Chart: Month by Month. Data: Yahoo Finance (^GSPC, month-end closes)

headline: Novartis buys Hexal and Eon Labs
text: This year Novartis bought Hexal, one of Germany's leading generic drug makers, and the American generics company Eon Labs for $8.29 billion. Its Sandoz division is now the second-largest generics group in the world.
imageCaption: A Novartis production site at Stein, Switzerland
